title: PreToolUse hook enforcing cli_lookup before repo CLI use
problem: Claude bypasses the CLAUDE.md rule requiring cli_lookup.py to be run before invoking any repo CLI tool for the first time in a session. The rule relies on Claude self-discipline and fails on familiar-looking tools (e.g. notes.py), causing wrong-flag errors and wasted turns. Memory/feedback alone is insufficient because the failure mode is autopilot — Claude does not consult memory before guessing flags it 'already knows'. A harness-enforced PreToolUse hook is the durable fix.
description: Add a PreToolUse Bash hook that blocks invocations of known repo CLI tools when cli_lookup.py has not been run for that tool earlier in the same session. The hook parses the bash command, identifies the target CLI tool (matching against the tool list known to cli_lookup.py — i.e. tools under scribe/, budgeter/, pipeline/, docs/reference/, hooks/), inspects the current session's transcript jsonl for a prior cli_lookup.py invocation naming that tool, and blocks with a clear message if no prior lookup exists. cli_lookup.py itself is exempt. The hook script lives in the repo at hooks/enforce_cli_lookup.py and is wired up via the PROJECT-LEVEL Claude Code settings file at .claude/settings.json in the repo root (NOT the user-global ~/.claude/settings.json). Project-level settings are merged with user-global settings by Claude Code, so this gives per-project enforcement while keeping the configuration committable in this repo.
scope: 1) Create hooks/enforce_cli_lookup.py: reads hook payload from stdin, extracts bash command, identifies invocations of known repo CLI tools, checks current session transcript (path derived from session_id in payload, located under ~/.claude/projects/<project-key>/<session-id>.jsonl) for a prior cli_lookup.py call naming that tool, exits non-zero with instructive message if missing, exit 0 otherwise. 2) Create or update .claude/settings.json at the REPO ROOT (project-level, NOT user-global) with a PreToolUse Bash matcher that runs hooks/enforce_cli_lookup.py. If .claude/settings.json already exists, merge the new hook entry without clobbering existing settings. 3) Source the tool list from cli_lookup.py (single source of truth) — either by importing it or by parsing its known-tool registry — so the hook does not duplicate tool names. 4) Add a brief test/verification: invoke a repo CLI without prior lookup (should block) and after a prior lookup (should pass). All file writes MUST be inside the repo working tree so the executor can git-commit them. Out of scope: editing ~/.claude/settings.json (user-global), changing CLAUDE.md wording, refactoring cli_lookup.py, hooks for non-Bash tools, modifying budgeter or other existing hooks.
context: CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: A previous attempt at this ticket failed because the plan put the settings.json edit at C:/Users/amedi/.claude/settings.json (outside the repo), and the executor's git commit had nothing to stage and aborted with 'Git error committing:'. This re-attempt MUST keep all file changes inside the repo working tree. Use the project-level .claude/settings.json in the repo root, which Claude Code merges with the user-global file automatically. Triggered by a real failure: Claude ran 'python scribe/notes.py list --limit 5' on autopilot when the actual flag is --last.
